# exome_gene_counts_v

Per-gene rare-variant COUNTS from exome studies whose release carries counts and a Bayesian
gene statistic but no p-value or effect size. First source: the Autism Sequencing Consortium
2026 release (dataset ASC2, trait ASD, 20,893 autosomal genes). LONG: one row per gene x
variant_class x inheritance_mode, so a gene has 7 x 3 = 21 rows. The two counts are the pair
the mode contrasts — de_novo: probands vs unaffected siblings; inherited: transmitted vs
untransmitted alleles; case_control: cases vs controls. They are the source's "independent"
counts (one variant per person per gene, LOFTEE-filtered inherited and case-control PTVs)
and do NOT equal sums over exome_variant_counts_v. THIS VIEW HAS NO TEST STATISTIC. The
gene's Bayes factor and FDR are in exome_gene_bayes_results_v on the same (dataset, trait,
gene_id); join there for "is this gene associated". Do not compute rate ratios, odds ratios
or p-values from these counts and present them as the study's result — the release reports
none. Every gene is present with every class and mode, zeros included, so a zero is a real
zero. The CNV classes DEL and DUP exist only here (no per-variant CNV rows). A literal `chr
= <n>` beside `gene =` keeps a query under the sandbox scan cap.

## Scan pruning

Partitioned on `chr`: a literal `chr = <n>` predicate is what keeps a query under the sandbox's per-query scan cap, which BigQuery checks against its partition-pruned estimate before running anything. Clustered on `dataset`, `gene`, `trait`: an equality on these cuts the bytes actually billed but does not lower that estimate, so it never substitutes for the partition predicate.

## Columns

| column | type | description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `dataset` | `STRING` | Study name (ASC2) |
| `trait` | `STRING` | Trait/phenotype name |
| `gene` | `STRING` | Gene symbol (ASC2: GENCODE v29 spelling) |
| `gene_id` | `STRING` | Ensembl gene ID (unversioned); the join key to exome_gene_bayes_results_v |
| `chr` | `INT64` | Chromosome number, chromosome X is 23. The partitioning column |
| `gene_start_pos` | `INT64` | Gene start position (GRCh38) |
| `gene_end_pos` | `INT64` | Gene end position (GRCh38) |
| `variant_class` | `STRING` | PTV, Mis2 (MPC >= 2 and AlphaMissense >= 0.97), Mis1 (one of the two), Mis0 (neither), synonymous, DEL, DUP |
| `inheritance_mode` | `STRING` | de_novo, inherited or case_control; decides what n_affected and n_unaffected count |
| `n_affected` | `INT64` | de_novo: variants in probands; inherited: alleles transmitted to probands; case_control: alleles in cases |
| `n_unaffected` | `INT64` | de_novo: variants in unaffected siblings; inherited: untransmitted alleles; case_control: alleles in controls |
| `trait_original` | `STRING` | Original trait name in the respective dataset (the phenotypes_v join key) |
| `resource` | `STRING` | Data source identifier (lowercase), derived from dataset in the view |

## Columns with a small, enumerable set of values

| column | scoped by |
| --- | --- |
| `resource` | — |
| `dataset` | `resource` |
| `variant_class` | `resource` |
| `inheritance_mode` | `resource` |

## Worked examples

Queries that run against exome_gene_counts_v as written.

### All 21 count rows for one gene — the evidence behind its Bayes factor. chr beside gene keeps the estimate under the cap.

```sql
SELECT variant_class, inheritance_mode, n_affected, n_unaffected
FROM exome_gene_counts_v
WHERE chr = 14 AND gene = 'CHD8' AND dataset = 'ASC2'
ORDER BY variant_class, inheritance_mode
```

### Genes with the most de novo PTVs in probands, with the gene's FDR joined on. Genome-wide, so no chr predicate; the narrow column list keeps it under the cap.

```sql
SELECT c.gene, c.n_affected AS de_novo_ptv_probands, c.n_unaffected AS de_novo_ptv_siblings,
       b.fdr, b.qc_flagged
FROM exome_gene_counts_v c
JOIN exome_gene_bayes_results_v b
  ON b.dataset = c.dataset AND b.trait = c.trait AND b.gene_id = c.gene_id
WHERE c.dataset = 'ASC2' AND c.variant_class = 'PTV' AND c.inheritance_mode = 'de_novo'
ORDER BY c.n_affected DESC
LIMIT 20
```
